sections.content: Debido a que and ya que introduce a cause before or after the main clause; por eso and como resultado de introduce a consequence, usually at the start of a new sentence. Historical writing leans on all four to explain why something happened, not just that it did. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Debido a que la población indígena del Caribe ya se había reducido drásticamente, los colonos recurrieron al tráfico de personas esclavizadas desde África.
items.english: Because the indigenous population of the Caribbean had already declined drastically, colonists increasingly turned to trafficking enslaved people from Africa.

items.spanish: Por eso, muchos historiadores consideran la caña de azúcar uno de los motores principales detrás del comercio transatlántico de esclavos.
items.english: That's why many historians consider sugarcane one of the main engines behind the transatlantic slave trade.

items.spanish: La población indígena no tenía ninguna inmunidad, ya que estos patógenos habían evolucionado junto a los animales domesticados de Eurasia.
items.english: The indigenous population had no immunity, since these pathogens had evolved alongside Eurasia's domesticated animals.

items.spanish: Como resultado de esta catástrofe demográfica, millones de hectáreas de tierras de cultivo volvieron a cubrirse de bosque.
items.english: As a result of this demographic catastrophe, millions of hectares of farmland became forest again.

sections.content: Debido a que and ya que both mean roughly "because," but ya que leans slightly more formal and often introduces a reason the reader should already find plausible. Por eso and como resultado de both mean "as a result," but como resultado de takes a noun phrase (como resultado de la crisis), while por eso stands alone at the start of a new sentence.
